purpose: Headless whole-file build of the genuine gameplay code, renderer, status bar and HUD, and the genuine sound logic (s_sound.c) and level-start melt (f_wipe.c), driven through the vanilla -playdemo path with a mirror of D_Display after every dumped tic; run in CI on synthetic WADs with the synthetic graphics and sound PWADs and locally on a real IWAD. Expected sound streams, frames, palette numbers, M_Random indices and messages come from the genuine code, never from Rust output and never from the independent Python models.

excluded.r_main_extract: not used: r_main.c is compiled whole
excluded.i_sound_c_platform: compiled whole, but I_InitSound (the /dev/dsp open and the sound-server popen), I_UpdateSound, I_SubmitSound and I_ShutdownSound are never called; the mixer harness is a separate tool

variant_notes.address: run with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 (leak detection disabled; not LeakSanitizer coverage); -fno-sanitize=alignment because z_zone.c rounds block sizes to 4 (z_zone.c:195) while the LP64 memblock_t needs 8-byte alignment

abi_adapters.reason: P_GroupLines: linebuffer holds total line_t pointers (8 bytes each on LP64); total*4 overruns the zone block and Z_CheckHeap (g_game.c:488) calls I_Error.
On-disk maptexture_t: a 4-byte field as on the 32-bit original, so patchcount is at byte 20 and patches at 22 (the driver checks the generated layout probe before running).
R_InitTextures: textures is a pointer array (texture_t**).
R_InitColormaps truncates a pointer to int; the runner does not call it, the file is adapted so it compiles LP64-clean (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line).

Z_ChangeTag: the owner test truncates the 64-bit user pointer to 32 bits, so a valid owner whose address has small low 32 bits (observed under ASan on the CI runner: W_CacheLumpNum re-caching the one patch lump) raises "an owner is required for purgable blocks"; the 32-bit original compares the whole pointer, which uintptr_t does on LP64 (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line).

sanitizer_adapters.reason: P_SpawnPlayer: ANG45 * q overflows int for quotients outside -4..3; the original targets wrap it modulo 2^32, which the unsigned product computes (same statement form as p_mobj.c:794).
P_SpawnMapThing: the declared M3h9b adapter (tools/reference/m3h9b_reference.py SANITIZER_ADAPTERS[0]).
P_RadiusAttack: the declared M3h9b adapter (tools/reference/m3h9b_reference.py SANITIZER_ADAPTERS[1]).

A_PosAttack: `int angle` holds the actor angle (angle_t converted to int) and the spread is added in int, which overflows for angles near the int limits; the original targets wrap it modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does (the P_Random subexpression is unchanged). Needed: the overflow build reports this statement on the synthetic chaos script.
A_SPosAttack: the same int sum as p_enemy.c:816; declared for robustness.
A_CPosAttack: the same int sum as p_enemy.c:816; declared for robustness.

P_DamageMobj: a telefrag (PIT_StompThing, p_map.c:105) passes damage 10000, so the int product damage*(FRACUNIT>>3)*100 overflows (it does for any damage >= 2622). The genuine strict (-fwrapv) and strict32 builds wrap it modulo 2^32 to -397,934,592 before the signed division; the unsigned product computes the same wrapped value without undefined behaviour and the (int) conversion is modulo on GCC; the division stays signed (decision I3, docs/M4B_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md section 2 T8.10).

render_abi_adapters.reason: R_InitTranslationTables truncates a pointer to int before aligning it to 256 (as r_data.c:642 does for colormaps); on LP64 the truncated pointer is invalid. intptr_t keeps the whole pointer (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line); strict32 compiles the genuine text, where int and pointers have the same width.

render_sanitizer_adapters.reason: R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle: finesine has 10240 entries (tables.c:584) and finetangent, 4096, immediately precedes it (tables.c:67; the driver checks this layout in strict and strict32), so the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finetangent[4096 + i] for a negative index i (from -4096 to -1: `int angleb>>ANGLETOFINESHIFT` of an angle sum whose top bit is set); the address build puts a redzone between the arrays and -fsanitize=bounds reports the index, so the adapter reads that element explicitly (finetangent[FINEANGLES/2 + i]). The three-variant frame identity shows it is the same value. Same form as r_main.c:485; declared for robustness.

R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle: finesine has 10240 entries (tables.c:584) and finetangent, 4096, immediately precedes it (tables.c:67; the driver checks this layout in strict and strict32), so the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finetangent[4096 + i] for a negative index i (from -4096 to -1: `int angleb>>ANGLETOFINESHIFT` of an angle sum whose top bit is set); the address build puts a redzone between the arrays and -fsanitize=bounds reports the index, so the adapter reads that element explicitly (finetangent[FINEANGLES/2 + i]). The three-variant frame identity shows it is the same value. Observed: index -218 on the BINF1 synthetic script in the Phase 1 prototype.

R_RenderSegLoop: angle is 0..8191 (an angle_t shifted right by ANGLETOFINESHIFT) while finetangent has 4096 entries; the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finesine[angle - 4096] for angle >= 4096 (finesine follows finetangent, tables.c:67, 584; checked by the driver), and the difference rw_offset - FixedMul(...) wraps modulo 2^32 under -fwrapv (observed overflow -70518787 - 2082184609 on TSPLIT, BVB1 and BARON1 in the prototype). The adapter reads the element explicitly and subtracts in unsigned arithmetic, converted back to fixed_t (modulo on GCC).

R_StoreWallRange: abs of an int difference that can be INT_MIN (observed on BTUNNEL in the prototype); the genuine strict and strict32 abs returns INT_MIN, which converts to 0x80000000 in the angle_t offsetangle; the adapter computes that value as an unsigned negation without the signed overflow.

R_StoreWallRange: the texture-mid sum overflows 32 bits on a high wall with a large row offset (observed in the address build on the real-map scripts M8IDLE and M8IDLE3 in the prototype, owner ruling on R12); the genuine strict and strict32 builds wrap it modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does.
R_StoreWallRange: as r_segs.c:603 for the lower texture (observed in the address build on the real-map script M9WALK in the prototype); the genuine builds wrap modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does.

R_DrawPlanes: index SCREENWIDTH of byte top[SCREENWIDTH]; visplane_t puts pad2 right after top (r_defs.h), which absorbs the write in every build. -fsanitize=bounds reports the array index; the subscript through a byte pointer is the same store.
R_DrawPlanes: index -1 of top[] lands in pad1 (r_defs.h); the same store through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads top[minx-1] (pad1, 0xff); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads bottom[minx-1] (pad3, 0 from static storage); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads top[maxx+1] (pad2, 0xff); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads bottom[maxx+1] (pad4, 0); the same load through a byte pointer.

R_DrawSpan: the texture coordinate sum overflows (observed -2145453427 + -11386560 on TELE1, SAWBITE, TELEZ, BOSS2, BTUNNEL in the prototype); only its low bits index the flat (r_draw.c:548-557); the genuine strict and strict32 builds wrap modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does. Line-keyed: r_draw.c:682 has the same text.
R_DrawSpan: as r_draw.c:559 for the other coordinate; the genuine builds wrap modulo 2^32. Line-keyed: the text is also a prefix of r_draw.c:683 (which ends with a space).
R_DrawSpanLow: the same sum as r_draw.c:559 (declared for robustness; low detail is refused, decision R2). Line-keyed: r_draw.c:559 has the same text.
R_DrawSpanLow: as r_draw.c:560 (declared for robustness; low detail is refused).

sound_abi_adapters.reason: glibc errno is thread-local and declared by <errno.h>; i_sound.c declares it itself (line 166), which does not link against glibc. Applied in every build (a libc adapter, not an LP64 one).
with <errno.h> the errno macro would turn this declaration into a conflicting declaration; myioctl (its only user) is reached only from I_InitSound, which the runner never calls.

driver_behaviour: The demo header selects skill, episode and map (g_game.c:1596-1598); the driver has no map argument.
I_Quit (vanilla exit(0), i_system.c:116-124) sets a flag and longjmps to the driver, so no statement after the call in G_CheckDemoStatus or G_Ticker runs, as with exit.

After each dumped tic the driver stops if gameaction is ga_completed, ga_victory or ga_worlddone (end=exit, set during P_Ticker by G_ExitLevel/G_SecretExitLevel, g_game.c:1002-1018): G_Ticker handles gameaction before reading the next ticcmd (g_game.c:617-652, 656-669), so the next call would run G_DoCompleted and enter the intermission (g_game.c:1133-1140), which the runner does not model; a demo that reaches its marker ends end=marker. WI_Start still aborts as a safety net.

After each dumped tic the driver also stops if a player in the game is PST_REBORN (end=reborn; P_DeathThink on BT_USE, p_user.c:227-228): the next G_Ticker would run its reborn loop (g_game.c:612-614), G_DoReborn would set ga_loadlevel (g_game.c:924-931) and the level would reload (g_game.c:621-623), outside the admitted domain (decision G11).
After every tic the driver calls the genuine Z_CheckHeap (z_zone.c:399-420), a read-only walk of the zone; vanilla calls it only in G_DoLoadLevel (g_game.c:488).

Linker-level observers (-Wl,--wrap): P_AddThinker gives each thinker a serial (T rows), P_SetThingPosition gives the thing a link serial (the global link order is the ascending current link serial), Z_Free of a known thinker records it as freed since the previous dump (K rows, in free order) and, for a removed mobj, a copy of the mobj taken before the genuine free (RM rows); P_InitThinkers (after Z_FreeTags at level setup) drops every entry (K rows with seq -1). K rows also carry adds, the P_AddThinker count at the free; a pending mobj (R row) is followed by an RR row with its M columns. Each of these wrappers only records and then calls the genuine function.

ZeroFill: the Z_Malloc wrapper zero-fills every block after the genuine allocation. Only values the original leaves undefined change: plat_t.count (EV_DoPlat, p_plats.c:173; read only in waiting after being set, p_plats.c:75, 84, 113, 120) and floormove_t.newspecial (EV_DoFloor, p_floor.c:282; set and read only for lowerAndChange and donutRaise, p_floor.c:231, 242, 422, 433, p_spec.c:1203) made the strict and address dumps differ. lowerAndChange without a neighbour at the destination height reads newspecial and texture uninitialised in vanilla (p_floor.c:242-243); the fill makes them 0 there.
--selftest-extra-draw TIC calls the public P_Random () once before G_Ticker of tic TIC (test only).
The zone is 6 MiB (vanilla mb_used, i_system.c:51) unless --zone-mb is given.

H rows end with secretexit (added for M4a): g_game.c's boolean secretexit (g_game.c:999), set by G_SecretExitLevel (g_game.c:1009-1018) and cleared by G_ExitLevel (g_game.c:1002-1006). New columns are appended at the end of their rows so every earlier column keeps its position.

R rows carry fn and sector (added for M4a): a -Wl,--wrap=P_RemoveThinker observer records, before the genuine P_RemoveThinker (p_tick.c:80-84) overwrites the function pointer, the kind of a removed non-mobj thinker (1 T_VerticalDoor, 2 T_PlatRaise, 3 T_MoveFloor, 4 T_MoveCeiling, 0 other) and its sector index, so a mover created and removed within one tic keeps its sector for the encoder; -1 when unknown.

M4b runner (tools/reference/m4b_build.py): the M4a driver text unchanged (no new dump column); one more declared sanitizer adapter, p_inter.c:817 (the telefrag thrust product in unsigned arithmetic), applied to the overflow and address builds only; strict and strict32 compile the genuine text.

L rows print line_t.flags with ML_MAPPED (256, doomdata.h:135) cleared (decision R5): R_StoreWallRange sets it on every wall it stores (r_segs.c:398) and only the automap (am_map.c:1128) and savegames (p_saveg.c:141) read it; the newly mapped lines of each frame travel in the frame stream (M rows). --no-mask-mapped (diagnostic) prints the genuine value.

Read-provenance tracker (decision R4 and its owner ruling): -Wl,--wrap observers of R_DrawColumn, R_DrawFuzzColumn and R_DrawSpan recompute every source index the genuine loop reads (r_draw.c:132-146) and classify it against the source block (the last R_GetColumn composite, or the cache block of the last W_CacheLumpNum lump) and, for composites, a written-byte mask replicated from R_GenerateLookup and R_DrawColumnInCache (r_data.c:184-216, 351-372) using W_ReadLump (never the zone); a per-pixel taint follows the never-cleared screen (spans clear it, fuzz copies it from the pixel it reads). Columns holding a tainted pixel are the frame's non-comparable columns; an unidentified source makes the whole frame non-comparable. The wrappers read genuine state only and then call the genuine drawer.

View record (--view FILE, schema DOOM-M5A-VIEW-v1, decision R6): per dumped tic, after the dump, the player's mobj x, y and angle, viewz, viewheight, deltaviewheight, bob, onground (p_user.c:51), extralight, fixedcolormap, the invisibility power, both psprites (state, tics, sx, sy) and the player's sector and light level, and the non-identity flat and texture translations (A rows).

Limits (decision R3): MAXDRAWSEGS and MAXVISSPRITES drop silently in the genuine code (r_segs.c:386-387, r_things.c:330-331) and are counted in the frame stream; R_FindPlane calls I_Error past MAXVISPLANES (r_plane.c:245-246) and R_DrawPlanes past MAXVISPLANES or MAXOPENINGS (r_plane.c:380-386), which the stub reports in an E row before it aborts; a write past visplanes (R_CheckPlane, r_plane.c:313-317), openings (R_StoreWallRange) or solidsegs (R_ClipSolidWallSegment, r_bsp.c:122-133), detected by the R_CheckPlane and R_StoreWallRange observers, is reported in an O row with its witness name and ends the run after that frame with end=refused.

Table layout (decision R12): in strict and strict32 (no table adapters) the driver refuses to run (status 9) unless finesine starts right after finetangent (tables.c:67, 584), the layout the genuine out-of-range reads of r_main.c:484-485 and r_segs.c:266 rely on.

M5b runner (tools/reference/m5b_build.py; decisions S1, S14-S17, S22 and S23 of docs/M5B_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md): the M5a driver text forked into tools/reference/m5b_driver.c; the 41 genuine files of the M5a runner with every M5a adapter, plus the genuine status bar and HUD whole (st_stuff.c st_lib.c hu_stuff.c hu_lib.c m_cheat.c), and tools/reference/m5b_stubs.c.

Sequence (M5b): V_Init (d_main.c:1012); Z_Init; W_InitMultipleFiles over the --wad files (map WAD, tests/reference/m5b_gfx.wad, demo lump); gamemode = registered; R_Init (d_main.c:1095); P_InitSwitchList; P_InitPicAnims; R_InitSprites on a NUMSPRITES+1 copy of sprnames with an explicit NULL terminator (as M5a); D_CheckNetGame single-player values; HU_Init (d_main.c:1110); ST_Init (d_main.c:1113); singledemo; the command source (G_DeferedPlayDemo, G_DoPlayDemo; ST_Start and HU_Start run inside the genuine P_SpawnPlayer for the console player, p_mobj.c:693-699); dump "load"; then { G_Ticker (whose GS_LEVEL case runs the genuine ST_Ticker and HU_Ticker after P_Ticker, g_game.c:729-734); gametic++; Z_CheckHeap; dump; view record; display } per tic.

Display (decision S14, finding FH2): with --render every, a mirror of D_Display (d_main.c:191-355) for GS_LEVEL without menu, automap, pause or wipe after the dump of every dumped tic, one display per tic as vanilla under -timedemo (singletics, d_main.c:375-395): R_ExecuteSetViewSize on the first display (setsizeneeded from R_Init, d_main.c:215-220); wipe = gamestate != wipegamestate (true on the first display only; the melt is not run, only its redrawsbar effect is mirrored, d_main.c:223-229, 242-243); HU_Erase (d_main.c:231-232); ST_Drawer (viewheight == 200, redrawsbar) (d_main.c:237-247); R_RenderPlayerView (d_main.c:267-268); HU_Drawer (d_main.c:270-271); R_FillBackScreen and the border block (d_main.c:278-295; both return at once at screenblocks 10 and 11, r_draw.c:746-747, 850-851); the state copies (d_main.c:297-300); NetUpdate (the stub). The frame is the whole 320x200 screens[0] after the display. The load (gametic 0) is never displayed; the end=exit and end=reborn tics are.

Record and mask (decision S16), in this runner only: the H row prints rndindex without the presentation draws, (rndindex - draws) & 0xff, the gameplay-only value every frozen runner prints (in single player rndindex is presentation state: its only gameplay reader is the netgame consistency check, g_game.c:680-692); the P row prints as message the pointer the genuine HU_Ticker found before it took and cleared it (hu_stuff.c:519-530; the frozen M4a stub's meaning). The genuine rndindex after every displayed tic (P rows of the frame stream) and every message HU_Ticker took with its code and text (X rows) are recorded and compared separately. --no-mask-rnd and --no-hu-record print the genuine values (diagnostic; the self-test shows the dump comparison then fails).

Palette: I_SetPalette is a declared stub whose hook records (PLAYPAL pointer offset) / 768 when the pointer lies on a 768-byte boundary inside the cached PLAYPAL lump (st_stuff.c:1045-1050); anything else is counted as unknown and must stay 0. ST_doPaletteStuff calls I_SetPalette only on a change (st_palette starts -1 from ST_initData, st_stuff.c:1266), so the P row carries both the current palette and the palette set during the frame (-1 if none).

Frame stream (--frames FILE, schema DOOM-M5B-FRAMES-v1, row kinds in frame_row_kinds): the M5a F row (the SHA-256 of the 64,000 bytes of screens[0], now after the whole display; the SHA-256 with tracker-flagged columns zeroed; fuzzpos; the renderer counters) and M, U, N, O, E rows as M5a; per frame a P row (tic, palette, palette_set, face index of w_faces at 143,168, message_on of the HUD message widget, genuine rndindex), X rows (each message HU_Ticker took: the tic, the message code of the dump, the text), a D row (diagnostic: M_Random draws inside and outside ST_Ticker so far, the 2D tracker counts of the frame, the SHA-256 with the rows below the view zeroed for the M5a comparison); at the end W rows (per status bar widget: calls, first, min and max value, changes) and a Z row of totals. --frames-raw DIR writes frame_NNNNN.raw (the whole frame) per frame.

Read-provenance tracker on the 2D drawers (decision S17, finding FH5): -Wl,--wrap observers of V_DrawPatch and V_DrawPatchDirect (v_video.c:210-262, 331-344) re-walk the posts the genuine loop reads and count a post byte outside its lump (the pixel is tainted with the lump's origin), a write below row 199 of the screen or row 31 of screens[4] (beyond_rows), and a patch the range check skips (v_video.c:221-232; skipped_patches); a V_CopyRect (v_video.c:165-195) from screens[4] copies a per-byte defined mask maintained by the patch observer, so a pixel copied from a screens[4] byte no patch wrote is an undefined read (bar_undef_px, origin BG:unset). Pixels written from defined bytes clear the screen taint. A frame with any of these counts other than a skipped patch is to be refused as a whole by the reference tool. Observed count on the committed items: see tests/reference/m5b_results.json.

AttackerRemoved (decision S17): the face reads plyr->attacker->x and ->y while damagecount is non-zero and the attacker is not the player (st_stuff.c:799-813), and the pointer is never cleared when its mobj is removed (p_inter.c:874; P_RemoveMobj, p_mobj.c). Before the genuine ST_Ticker the driver checks that such an attacker is still in the thinker list (a pending removal stays allocated until P_RunThinkers frees it, p_tick.c:117-128); if not, it writes the witness AttackerRemoved (an O row), skips the genuine ST_Ticker and ends the run before that tic is dumped (end=refused).

The command source (decision S3, step 7b kept apart): a version-110 demo lump played through the genuine -playdemo path (G_DeferedPlayDemo, G_DoPlayDemo; each tic's command read by the genuine G_Ticker through G_ReadDemoTiccmd, g_game.c:656-669, 1484-1504). It is the only command source of DOOM-M5B-RUNNER-v1; the driver keeps it behind command_source_begin and command_before_tic so that a later, separately declared mode can be added without changing what this one means.

The bespoke scenario (decision S1): --bespoke-keys TIC TEXT posts a key-down and a key-up event for every character of TEXT to the genuine G_Responder (g_game.c:504-580) before G_Ticker of tic TIC, where D_ProcessEvents runs in the -timedemo loop (d_main.c:375-383). M_Responder, which D_ProcessEvents calls first (d_main.c:161-177), returns false for a letter key while no menu, message or save string is up (m_menu.c:1349-1617); HU_Responder does nothing with a letter outside a netgame (hu_stuff.c:654-700); AM_Responder (stub) returns false, as am_map.c:625-633 does for every key but AM_STARTKEY while the automap is off. Used only for the cheats iddqd (the god face, st_stuff.c:549-560, 870-882) and idbeholds (the berserk term of the palette, st_stuff.c:636-648, 1008-1016), which wire 24 never reaches; the scenario's dumps are not compared with any frozen digest.

Configurations (decision S14): screenblocks 10 and 11, detail 0, are compared; --screenblocks 3..11 is accepted as in M5a; --detail 1 is refused with status 8 before anything loads; R_DrawColumnLow, R_DrawSpanLow and R_DrawTranslatedColumn abort if ever reached.

Test and diagnostic options (never touching genuine code text): --selftest-pixel TIC X Y (after R_RenderPlayerView, as M5a), --selftest-bar TIC X Y (flips the low bit of one screens[0] pixel after the display of tic TIC), --selftest-palette TIC and --selftest-rnd TIC (the P row of tic TIC records the value with its low bit flipped), --selftest-message TIC (a message taken at tic TIC is recorded one tic late), --diag-fill N (fills screens[0] with N after V_Init: frames that do not change show that every pixel is written before it is shown), --lump-trace FILE (each lump name the genuine code looks up).

M5c runner (tools/reference/m5c_build.py; docs/M5C_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md sections 3.1 and 3.4): the M5b driver text forked into tools/reference/m5c_driver.c; the 46 genuine files of the M5b runner with every M5a and M5b adapter, plus s_sound.c and f_wipe.c whole and unmodified and i_sound.c whole with the two errno lines of sound_abi_adapters, and tools/reference/m5c_stubs.c (the M5b stubs without S_Start, S_StartSound, S_StopSound, S_PauseSound, S_ResumeSound and S_ChangeMusic, plus I_ReadScreen, the genuine memcpy of i_video.c:527-530, which f_wipe.c calls).

Sequence (M5c): as M5b, plus: under --handle integrated, after R_InitSprites, the data loop of I_InitSound (i_sound.c:799-813, I_Init at d_main.c:1101) with the genuine getsfx; the M_LoadDefaults values with no config file (snd_SfxVolume 8, snd_MusicVolume 8, numChannels 3); after the D_CheckNetGame values, the genuine S_Init (8, 8) (d_main.c:1107), its channel table captured as the one Z_Malloc block it allocates (s_sound.c:179-180; size checked against numChannels * sizeof (channel_t)); S_Start inside the genuine P_SetupLevel (p_setup.c:607). Per tic: G_Ticker; gametic++; S_UpdateSounds (players[consoleplayer].mo) (d_main.c:383-395, singletics) under --update-schedule tic, or only after the tics at which a 512-frame buffer is due under --update-schedule buffer; Z_CheckHeap; dump; view record; display.

The M_Random contract (M5c; replaces decision S15 of the M5b runner): sound and the level-start melt draw as the genuine engine does. The M_Random observer counts the draws of S_StartSound (s_sound.c:327-346), of ST_Ticker (st_stuff.c:992) and of the melt (wipe_initMelt, f_wipe.c:159-166) separately; any other draw is counted as other and must stay 0. The S16 mask of the H row subtracts every presentation draw ((rndindex - draws) & 0xff), so the game dumps keep the frozen meaning; the P rows of the frame stream carry the genuine rndindex.

The wipe (--wipe genuine, default): on the first display after the level load (gamestate != wipegamestate, d_main.c:223-229) the D_Display mirror calls wipe_StartScreen before drawing (d_main.c:226) and, after the drawing and the state copies, wipe_EndScreen and wipe_ScreenWipe (wipe_Melt) until done (d_main.c:320-344), with the declared counter I_GetTime; I_UpdateNoBlit, M_Drawer and I_FinishUpdate inside the loop are presentation and not run. The frame kept is the screen after the melt. With --render none the melt still runs at the same point (vanilla always displays). --wipe none keeps the M5b wipe-free display.

Handle convention (--handle integrated, default): the I_StartSound observer returns the genuine addsfx (id, vol, steptable[pitch], sep) exactly as i_sound.c:490-499 compiles with doomdef.h:84 commented out (configuration_adapters); --handle sndserv calls the compiled I_StartSound (i_sound.c:482-489). Every other sound observer records and calls the genuine function unchanged.

Start classification without touching s_sound.c: the S_StartSound observer snapshots the channel table and, when origin && origin != players[consoleplayer].mo (s_sound.c:304), calls the genuine global S_AdjustSoundParams once as a probe (pure but for R_PointToAngle2's viewx/viewy writes, r_main.c:384-385, which the genuine call repeats with the same values; no M_Random draw). Outcomes: link_volume (s_sound.c:283-290), inaudible (probe 0, s_sound.c:318-319), started (I_StartSound called), no_channel (S_getChannel -1, s_sound.c:352-355). Each start is cross-checked against the source (draw count, I_StartSound volume and separation against the probe or 8 and 128, the channel holding the handle); a disagreement is counted as mismatch and must stay 0. Stopped channels are found by diffing the snapshot and classified same_origin, priority, remove, level_start, finished or inaudible.

Sound stream (--sound-out FILE, schema DOOM-M5C-SOUND-v1, row kinds in sound_row_kinds): S per game S_StartSound call, T per game S_StopSound call, K per channel stopped, C per occupied channel after each S_UpdateSounds, L per I_GetSfxLumpNum, R per tic (rndindex after P_Ticker, after ST_Ticker and after the display; cumulative sound, status bar and melt draws; whether S_UpdateSounds ran and how many channels were occupied), W the melt, E an I_Error, Z totals. The stream does not depend on the screen size.

Frame stream (M5c): DOOM-M5C-FRAMES-v1 when sound or the wipe is on (the M5b row kinds plus Q, the frame digest with the rectangle any face patch can cover at 143,168 zeroed, and V, the melt picture after each wipe_ScreenWipe call, evidence only), with a #config-m5c line of the switches; with --sound off --wipe none exactly the M5b stream (DOOM-M5B-FRAMES-v1).
Test option (M5c): --selftest-sound TIC records the volume of the first started sound at or after tic TIC with its low bit flipped (the sound comparison must report that one row).
